tasks.short: Analyse cost and revenue trends per site and commitments, project next quarters, advise the Finance Director.

today.trigger: Quarterly reforecast, a budget round, or a question from the Finance Director (e.g. what a new warehouse client or a CAO wage rise does to margin).
steps: Export ledger, cost centre and customer revenue data from AFAS into Excel
Pull flex worker hours and invoices from the three agency portals
Collect lease, rent and customer contract terms from SharePoint
Build trend lines and driver assumptions per site in Excel
Write a short memo or slide with the projection and advice
drudgery: Re-exporting and re-mapping the same AFAS data every quarter
Matching agency invoices to cost centres by hand
Reading contracts again to find indexation clauses and end dates
today.time_sinks: Most hours go into gathering and cleaning data from AFAS and the agency portals before any analysis starts; the analysis itself is a fraction.

lenses.faster: Data pulls, the cost-centre mapping and the contract-term table become a fixed pipeline; a model drafts the trend narrative and first projection, so the accountant spends their time on the assumptions and the advice, cutting the task by about 40%.
lenses.autonomous: The nightly AFAS extract and monthly agency data refresh a driver model; after each close a model drafts a trend note per site, and the accountant reviews it before it goes to the Finance Director.
lenses.ambitious: Margin projections per warehouse customer each month instead of once a year, for the commercial team pricing renewals; demand would grow as it gets cheaper because every tender and renewal needs one.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss re-building the Excel export each quarter; the accountant wants more time on why Venlo's cost per order line moves and what to advise.
lenses.options: Running three scenarios (flex share high or low, CAO rise at 3% or 5%, a client lost or won) side by side changes the advice the Finance Director gives, not just the effort.
lenses.altitude: The week shifts from building spreadsheets to challenging drivers with site managers and FP&A; the accountant gains the right to set and sign off the driver assumptions, and the job becomes more expert.
reach: FP&A Analyst: rolling forecast updates per site (needs driver-based modelling and Power BI skills)
Controller: first draft of the quarterly outlook memo (needs to learn the board reporting format)

tasks.human_edge: Knowing which trend is real and which is a one-off (a lost client, a strike week, a peak season shift), and judging what the business can credibly commit to; a model adds unnoticed assumptions.
tasks.pattern_why: Data collection and the projection arithmetic are fixed software; one model call turns the numbers and contract notes into a checkable draft narrative inside that flow.

in_practice.trigger: Month close completed in AFAS, or a scenario request from the Finance Director.
steps: Pipeline loads AFAS ledger, cost centre and revenue data plus agency hours into the driver model
Contract terms (indexation, end dates) are kept in a table that a model extracts from SharePoint contracts once, then checked by a person
Model drafts trend analysis and a base projection per site with stated assumptions
Accountant reviews assumptions, adjusts, and writes the advice
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant approves every assumption and the projection before it reaches the Finance Director or FP&A.
data_needed: General ledger and cost centre actuals
Flex worker hours and agency invoices
Lease, rent and customer contract terms
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint finance folder: projection workbook with an assumptions log and the model draft kept next to the approved version.

evidence.claim: Accountants using AI closed the month 7.5 days faster and served 55% more clients a week in 79 small and mid-sized firms.
Multi-step reasoning errors are over half of the leading model's errors on accounting tasks; judgement is the bottleneck.

risks: Model adds an assumption nobody notices, so the projection cannot be rebuilt
Agency portal data formats change and the pipeline breaks silently
Advice reads more certain than the data supports
research_questions: Can the three agency portals deliver hours and invoices in a stable export or API, or only PDFs?
How far off were last year's projections, and which driver caused most of the error?
Do the Finance Director and FP&A accept a model-drafted narrative if the assumptions log is attached?

tasks.short: Check AFAS data for weak controls, duplicate payments, odd bank changes and agency overbilling.

today.trigger: Quarterly internal control review, auditor request, or a suspicion raised by AP or a site manager.
steps: Export AP invoices, vendor master changes and payments from AFAS
Sample transactions in Excel and look for duplicates and odd amounts
Compare agency invoices against ordered and approved hours
Check user roles in AFAS against segregation of duties
Write findings for the Controller
drudgery: Sampling by hand instead of testing every transaction
Re-checking the same vendor IBAN changes every quarter
Matching agency invoices to hours line by line
today.time_sinks: Exporting and sampling; only a small sample gets checked, so most of the time buys little coverage.

lenses.faster: Rule-based tests run over every AP line, payment and vendor change, so sampling disappears; the accountant only reviews flagged items, about half the time it takes today.
lenses.autonomous: After each payment batch and each night's AFAS refresh, tests for duplicate invoices, IBAN changes followed by payment, segregation-of-duties conflicts and agency hours above ordered hours run on their own and queue exceptions.
lenses.ambitious: Weekly checks of agency invoices against approved hours for all 150 to 300 flex workers, which today get only a spot check; this would grow with the flex pool in peak season.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss manual sampling in Excel; the accountant wants more time investigating the real anomalies and fixing the control behind them.
lenses.options: Not a drafting task; thresholds are tuned, not chosen between drafts.
lenses.altitude: The accountant designs and maintains the test library and decides which flags become findings; the job becomes more expert, closer to an internal auditor.
reach: Bookkeeper: duplicate-invoice checks before payment (needs the AP workflow in AFAS)
Controller: quarterly control self-assessment (needs control framework knowledge)

tasks.human_edge: Judging intent and context behind a flag, talking to the people involved, and deciding when a pattern is fraud or a sloppy process; interviews stay human.
tasks.pattern_why: Duplicate, IBAN-change, segregation-of-duties and hours-versus-invoice tests are rules that can be written down and run without a model.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly AFAS refresh and each Rabobank payment batch.
steps: Scripts test every AP invoice, payment and vendor master change against the rule set
Agency invoice lines are matched to approved hours from the portals
Exceptions land in a queue with the evidence attached
Accountant reviews exceptions and escalates real findings to the Controller
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant decides which exceptions are findings; payment holds and any accusation need the Controller.
data_needed: Agency orders, approved hours and invoices
in_practice.logs_to: Exception register in SharePoint with test name, evidence, reviewer and outcome.

evidence.claim: Full-population tests (duplicates, segregation of duties, IBAN changes) fit deterministic software at high autonomy; this is model knowledge, no product named in the digest.

risks: Too many false positives and the queue gets ignored
Test data includes personal data of flex workers; AVG purpose limitation and access rights apply
Rules go stale when AFAS workflows change
research_questions: Does AFAS expose the vendor master change log and user roles through a GetConnector?
How many duplicate or overbilled agency invoices did last year's manual checks find?
What false-positive rate can the reviewer handle weekly?

tasks.short: Build site budgets and produce the monthly budget-versus-actual report with explanations.

today.trigger: Month close for the report; the annual budget round in autumn.
steps: Export actuals per cost centre from AFAS
Paste into the budget-versus-actual Excel per site
Ask site and department managers to explain big variances by mail
Write the variance commentary
Publish to Power BI or mail the pack
drudgery: Copying actuals into the template each month
Writing the same type of commentary for small variances
today.time_sinks: Chasing explanations from site managers and writing commentary for every line over threshold.

lenses.faster: The variance table is computed straight from the AFAS extract and a model drafts commentary using last month's notes and known drivers; the accountant checks and adds what only managers know, saving about 55%.
lenses.autonomous: When close is marked done, the report builds itself, a model drafts commentary and pre-filled questions go to managers in Teams; the accountant approves before publishing.
lenses.ambitious: Weekly cost-versus-budget for each site manager in Tilburg, Venlo and Rotterdam, focused on flex labour and overtime, who today see it monthly and late; demand grows if it is cheap.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses copy-paste into templates; the accountant wants more time on the few variances that matter and on the budget conversation itself.
lenses.options: For the budget round, two or three versions (flex share, volume per client) change what the Finance Director approves.
lenses.altitude: The accountant owns the variance thresholds and driver definitions and decides which variances go to the Controller; the week moves from producing the pack to discussing it, a more expert role.
reach: FP&A Analyst: monthly variance pack (needs driver-based budgeting)
Controller: first draft of management commentary (needs board-level writing)

tasks.human_edge: Knowing the operational reason behind a variance (a client's volume dip, a sick-leave spike, a delayed invoice) and when to push back on a manager's explanation.
tasks.pattern_why: The comparison is plain software; one model call per report turns numbers plus manager notes into checkable commentary.

in_practice.trigger: Month close marked complete in AFAS.
steps: Pipeline computes budget versus actual per site and cost centre from the AFAS extract
Variances over threshold get a draft explanation and a question to the manager in Teams
Model drafts commentary from numbers and manager replies
Accountant edits and approves; pack publishes to Power BI
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant approves the commentary before the pack is published.
in_practice.logs_to: Power BI report with commentary version history in SharePoint.

evidence.claim: Management reports and budget against actual fit deterministic software with model-written commentary, autonomy 3.
AI use was linked to a 7.5-day faster close in 79 firms.

risks: Commentary sounds plausible but invents a reason
Managers stop answering when questions become automated
Budget structure in AFAS differs from Excel structure
research_questions: Is the budget held in AFAS or only in Excel?
How long does the monthly pack take today, and how much is chasing managers?
Would site managers use a weekly flex-labour cost view?

tasks.short: Audit payroll against the ledger, wage tax return, WW premium rates, pension and agency liability.

today.trigger: Monthly payroll close, the year-end, or an auditor or tax office question.
steps: Reconcile the AFAS payroll journal to the general ledger
Check wage tax return (loonaangifte) totals against payroll
Check contract types against the low or high WW premium
Check pension and CAO premiums and the WKR free space
Check agency invoices for chain liability (G-account share)
drudgery: Ticking payroll totals against the ledger by hand
Checking contract types one by one
today.time_sinks: Checking contract type versus WW premium and reconciling the loonaangifte with the ledger.

lenses.faster: Tie-outs and premium checks run every month over all employees; the accountant reviews only differences, saving about 45%.
lenses.autonomous: After each payroll run, scripts reconcile payroll to ledger and loonaangifte, flag contracts on low WW premium that should be high (e.g. ended within two months), and check agency G-account shares; the accountant reviews the flags.
lenses.ambitious: A monthly check on the 150 to 300 flex workers' agency invoices for chain-liability and correct CAO rates, a group checked only at year-end today; demand grows with seasonal peaks.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss ticking totals; the accountant wants more time resolving the real premium and liability issues with the Payroll Specialist.
lenses.options: Not much; checks produce one answer per rule.
lenses.altitude: The accountant owns the payroll control set and signs off on premium positions before the auditor sees them; more expert, closer to a payroll tax specialist.
reach: Payroll Specialist: monthly payroll-to-ledger reconciliation (needs AFAS payroll module knowledge)
HR Administrator: contract-type data quality checks (needs CAO contract rules)

tasks.human_edge: Interpreting tax and premium rules in borderline cases, deciding on a correction with the tax office, and handling sensitive payroll data with care.
tasks.pattern_why: Tie-outs and WW premium rules are explicit; they run without a model.

steps: Scripts reconcile payroll journal to ledger and loonaangifte
Contract types are checked against the WW premium applied
Agency invoices are checked for G-account split
Accountant reviews differences and agrees corrections with the Payroll Specialist
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant and Payroll Specialist approve any correction; tax office contact stays with the Controller.
in_practice.logs_to: Payroll control file in SharePoint, restricted access.

evidence.claim: Payroll checks fit deterministic tests over every transaction at autonomy 4.

risks: AVG: payroll data access must be restricted and logged
Rule changes in WW premium law not updated in the scripts
Works council may want to know about automated checks on employee data
research_questions: Which AFAS payroll fields are reliable enough for contract-type checks?
How many WW premium corrections were made in the last two years?
Does the OR need to be consulted on these automated checks?

tasks.short: Advise HR and management on pay cost, benefits, WKR, AFAS set-up and tax planning.

today.trigger: A question from HR, the Finance Director or a project (CAO increase, new benefit, AFAS change).
steps: Clarify the question in a meeting or mail
Gather payroll and cost data from AFAS
Look up rules (WKR, CAO, tax)
Calculate effects in Excel
Write an advice memo
drudgery: Re-building cost models for each question
today.time_sinks: Building calculations and reading rules for each new question.

lenses.faster: A copilot finds the relevant rules and drafts the cost model and memo; the accountant checks and adapts, about 25% faster.
lenses.autonomous: Mostly ad hoc; the only standing piece is a monthly WKR free-space monitor that warns HR before the limit is passed.
lenses.ambitious: Cost-of-benefit advice for HR Business Partners for every new benefit or CAO proposal, a service they ask for rarely today; demand would grow.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses re-reading rules; the accountant wants more time in the advice conversation.
lenses.options: Several benefit or pay scenarios side by side change the HR decision.
lenses.altitude: The accountant becomes the go-to finance advisor for HR; more expert.
reach: Compensation and Benefits Specialist: cost modelling of benefits (needs CAO and benefit knowledge)
HR Business Partner: cost questions on reorganisation (needs HR context)

tasks.human_edge: Understanding what the asker really needs, weighing works council and employee impact, and taking responsibility for tax advice.
tasks.pattern_why: Questions vary; the person leads and AI helps with research and drafts.

in_practice.trigger: An advice request from HR or management.
steps: Accountant states the question in the copilot
Copilot gathers rules and data and drafts a cost model
Accountant checks and writes the advice
Advice is shared and discussed

evidence.claim: AFAS Jonas assists in tax returns; the user remains responsible for the check.
Tax estimates belong on a mandatory human review list.

risks: Wrong rule found by the copilot
Personal data in prompts
Advice taken as final without review
research_questions: How many advice requests come in per year, and from whom?
Is the WKR free space exceeded today?
Which copilot tool is allowed under the AVG policy?

tasks.short: Test new or changed systems before go-live: AFAS changes, agency links, e-invoicing.

today.trigger: A system project: AFAS workflow change, new agency interface, e-invoicing preparation.
steps: Read the specs
Write test cases and a control matrix
Run tests in the AFAS test environment
Report issues to the project
Sign off or block go-live
today.time_sinks: Writing test cases and documenting outcomes.

lenses.faster: AI drafts test cases and the control matrix from the specs and logs results; the accountant runs key tests and judges, about 30% faster.
lenses.autonomous: Limited; repeatable tests (posting, VAT codes, tie-outs) can run on each AFAS update in the test environment.
lenses.ambitious: A readiness check for Dutch e-invoicing (B2B from 2030) for the Controller, a project nobody owns yet; demand grows as the law firms up.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses writing test scripts; the accountant wants more say in system design.
lenses.options: Different test designs change what risks get covered.
lenses.altitude: The accountant becomes the finance voice in IT projects with a go-live veto; more expert.
reach: People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: testing AFAS HR changes (needs HR module knowledge)
Controller: e-invoicing project lead (needs project skills)

tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a control really works in daily practice and having the authority to block a go-live.
tasks.pattern_why: Every project differs; the person leads, AI drafts tests and documents.

steps: Copilot drafts test cases and controls from specs
Accountant reviews and runs tests
Results are logged automatically
Accountant signs off or blocks

evidence.claim: Dutch B2B e-invoicing from 1 July 2030, reporting from 2031, not yet law.
Intra-EU invoices due within 10 days under ViDA; domestic application still open.

risks: Test cases miss edge cases
Specs are incomplete
Go-live pressure overrides findings
research_questions: How many system changes per year need finance testing?
Does AFAS have a usable test environment?
Who owns e-invoicing readiness today?

tasks.short: Report asset use and audit findings to management with recommendations.

today.trigger: Quarterly management meeting or end of an audit.
steps: Collect asset register from AFAS
Gather usage data from sites
Summarise audit findings
Write report and recommendations
Present to management
today.time_sinks: Collecting usage data from sites and writing the report.

lenses.faster: A model drafts the report from the asset register, findings and usage data; the accountant edits and presents, about 35% faster.
lenses.autonomous: Quarterly the data is gathered and a draft report prepared for review.
lenses.ambitious: Asset use per site (forklifts, trucks) every month for site managers, so they can return or redeploy equipment; demand grows.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses formatting; the accountant wants more time on the recommendations.
lenses.options: Different recommendation sets (sell, redeploy, lease) change the decision.
lenses.altitude: The accountant shapes asset decisions with management; more expert.
reach: Controller: asset part of management report (needs presentation skills)
FP&A Analyst: capex review (needs investment appraisal)

tasks.human_edge: Choosing what to recommend and how to bring it to management.
tasks.pattern_why: Data is fixed; one model call drafts the report.

steps: Pipeline gathers asset register and findings
Model drafts the report
Accountant edits and approves
Report goes to management

evidence.claim: AI-prepared work stays under human review responsibility.

risks: Usage data missing or not in AFAS
Draft overstates findings
research_questions: Where is equipment usage data held (fleet telematics, WMS)?
How often does management act on asset recommendations today?

role.altitude: From preparing reconciliations, samples and reports by hand to designing the tests, tie-outs and driver models that check every entry, and judging the exceptions and advice that follow.
reach: Bookkeeper: duplicate and agency invoice checks
FP&A Analyst: variance pack and rolling forecast drafts
Controller: control self-assessment and e-invoicing readiness
role.ceiling_note: Limited by data access (agency portals, usage data outside AFAS), AVG rules on payroll data, and the need for human sign-off on tax, audit findings and advice; Dutch GAAP and VAT are not covered by any benchmark yet.
skills_to_grow: Writing rule-based tests and queries on AFAS data
Reviewing model output for hidden assumptions
Dutch payroll tax and WW premium rules
role.ambitious_version: The two accountants run a continuous control and insight service: every transaction, payroll run and agency invoice tested daily, weekly cost views for each site, and finance advice to HR on every pay and benefit decision, helping cut days to close and audit adjustments.
